item.title: Composite midpoint rule on a uniform grid
item.statement:
Input real numbers $a<b$, an integer $n\ge1$, and a real-valued function
$f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ evaluable at every point of $[a,b]$. Put
$h=(b-a)/n$ and $m_j=a+(j+\tfrac12)h$ for $0\le j<n$. The composite midpoint
rule returns

$$Q_M(f;a,b,n):=h\sum_{j<n} f(m_j).$$

The sum is the finite sum of [[def-finite-sum]]. The admissibility conditions
$a<b$ and $n\ge1$ ensure $h>0$ and all $m_j\in(a+jh,a+(j+1)h)$. If an input
fails either condition, the procedure returns invalid-grid; it makes no
quadrature claim for that input. The rule is an exact-real formula; floating
point evaluation and summation error are separate from its quadrature error.
item.strategy: A finite exact-real weighted sum; invalid intervals or panel counts return an explicit status.

references.title: Art B. Owen, Monte Carlo Theory, Methods and Examples, Chapter 7, §7.1
Tobin A. Driscoll and Richard J. Braun, Fundamentals of Numerical Computation, §5.6

item.title: Age-cohort quadrature along exact characteristics
item.statement: Approximate the initial age density by positive midpoint cohorts, transport cohort ages exactly, update cohort survival by forward Euler, and insert each time-step birth quadrature as a new age-zero cohort with explicit CFL and cutoff statuses.

item.title: Midpoint quadrature defect for one-dimensional P1 stiffness
item.statement: For a C2 scalar coefficient and continuous piecewise-linear functions on an interval partition, replacing each exact stiffness integral by its cell midpoint value changes the bilinear form by at most h squared times the coefficient second-derivative bound divided by 24 and the two derivative norms.
item.strategy: Apply the composite midpoint error on each cell to the C2 integrand A times the constant cell derivatives, convert cell sup norms to L2 norms, and sum.

references.title: Art B. Owen, Monte Carlo Theory, Methods and Examples, Chapter 7, Theorem 7.1
Tobin A. Driscoll and Richard J. Braun, Fundamentals of Numerical Computation, §5.6 Numerical Integration

item.title: One midpoint sample destroys a quadratic stiffness coercivity bound
item.statement: On a single interval with the one-dimensional P2 zero-boundary trial function x times (1 minus x), exact stiffness is positive but one midpoint sample gives zero discrete stiffness, so the first Strang stability hypothesis fails.
item.strategy: Compute the exact derivative integral and the midpoint derivative value.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part VI, Chapter 27, Error analysis with variational crimes
Joachim Schöberl, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Chapter 25, Non-conforming Finite Element Methods
